title: al-Kāfiya between India and Istanbul
summary: Ibn al-Ḥājib's compact syntax, read with Jāmī's commentary from the Ottoman lands to India.

sections.heading: The book
paragraphs: Al-Kāfiya, the sufficient, covers naḥw in a dense prose matn: the noun and its iʿrāb, the verb, the particle. Its brevity invited commentaries, the deepest by Raḍī al-Dīn al-Astarābādhī.
Jāmī's al-Fawāʾid al-ḍiyāʾiyya became the commentary of the madrasa, with its own glosses by ʿIṣām al-Dīn, Muḥarram Efendi and others.

sections.heading: Where it is read
paragraphs: In the Ottoman madrasa al-Kāfiya with Molla Câmî follows Birgivī's two books; in the Dars-i Niẓāmī, Sharḥ Jāmī follows Hidāyat al-naḥw.
